az_convention: index k = azimuth k*360/n_az deg from local north, clockwise toward east

sites.name: Connecting Ridge, best-lit point
sites.note: Ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters. Best-lit point at 2 m height in Glaser et al. 2018. Blue Origin's Blue Moon MK1 pathfinder also targets this ridge.
sites.source: Glaser et al. 2018, Planetary and Space Science 162, Table 2 (NTRS 20170007365)
sites.terrain: LOLA 20 m near field, 80 m and 240 m far field

sites.name: Shackleton crater rim
sites.note: High point on the Shackleton rim, close to the pole.
sites.source: Glaser et al. 2018, Planetary and Space Science 162, Table 2 (NTRS 20170007365)
sites.terrain: LOLA 20 m near field, 80 m and 240 m far field

sites.name: Peak near Shackleton (Bussey point D)
sites.note: Most-lit point of 2020 in Bussey et al. 2010. China's Chang'e 7 targets this area (launch now planned for 2027).
sites.source: Bussey et al. 2010, Icarus 208, abstract
sites.terrain: LOLA 20 m near field, 80 m and 240 m far field

sites.name: de Gerlache crater rim (GR1)
sites.note: High-illumination region of interest on the de Gerlache rim.
sites.source: De Rosa et al. 2012, Planetary and Space Science 74, Table 2 (arXiv 1208.5587)
sites.terrain: LOLA 20 m near field, 80 m and 240 m far field

sites.name: Malapert peak (MP1)
sites.note: Summit of the Malapert massif, about 5 km high, with a wide view toward Earth.
sites.source: De Rosa et al. 2012, Planetary and Space Science 74, Table 2 (arXiv 1208.5587)
sites.terrain: LOLA 20 m near field, 80 m and 240 m far field

sites.name: Geographic south pole
sites.note: The pole sits on the inner slope of Shackleton crater. Shown for reference.
sites.source: Definition
sites.terrain: LOLA 20 m near field, 80 m and 240 m far field

sites.terrain: LOLA 20 m near field, 80 m and 240 m far field

sites.name: Athena (IM-2), Mons Mouton

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram, Statio Shiv Shakti
sites.note: ISRO lander, first soft landing at high southern latitude. Outside the 80S terrain product, so terrain is from the 240 m model.
sites.source: LROC image 1314; IAU Gazetteer, Statio Shiv Shakti
sites.terrain: LOLA 240 m
